steps.what: 8c. Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding: any listener can veto the win check while it returns true; the sim has no such hook
steps.issue: ADDED 2026-07-26 in the power tier's review fix pass, for the same reason as step 8b: the engine-wide absence was prose-only (.superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 3c) and had no engine-level owner, so it reached neither audit_status nor the gap queue. C# SIDE: the win check returns false while `Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding(_state)` is true (CombatManager.cs:196), and Hook.cs:2442-2452 dispatches it to EVERY listener from IterateHookListeners, deliberately OUTSIDE the IsOverOrEnding gate -- Hook.cs:2436-2441's own comment says "Dispatched directly, not through the IterateCombatHookListeners guard: it is a predicate that drives the decision of whether combat ends, so suppressing it while combat is ending would drop the votes it collects." Five non-mock powers override it, and all five are ported: AdaptablePower.cs:53-56, InfestedPower, SteamEruptionPower.cs:23-26, StockPower, SurprisePower. SIM SIDE: hooks.py defines no `should_stop_combat_from_ending`; combat.py:272-277's `_all_enemies_dead` decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies, and there is no other veto point anywhere in the loop. DORMANT, and the dormancy is per-power rather than structural: each of the five ported overrides is paired with either a death prevention (adaptable, steam_eruption) or a mid-death spawn/retention that already keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own. NAMED TRIGGER: porting -- or writing -- a power that wants to hold combat open WITHOUT also preventing a death or adding a creature; it would have nothing to hook. The mechanism already carries `gap` at its five per-power sites (power/adaptable, power/infested, power/steam_eruption, power/stock, power/surprise); this step is its engine-level home, same verdict per rule 3. BOUNDARY: the READ site (CombatManager.cs:196) belongs to the turn_structure seam, which this pass does not own; what this step records is the missing hook SURFACE, filed next to the death/escape power-strip machinery this record already owns at steps 8 and 8b. CombatManager.cs is hashed by audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json and Hook.cs by this record, so drift is detected on both.

So no ported card can distinguish "result pile" from "discard pile" on this path, and the divergence stays a deliberate simplification rather than a gap. It becomes a gap the moment any Unplayable+Exhaust card is ported. The Play-pile transit it also skips is guard N9's missing Play pile.

The one place C# keeps the two apart is CardEnergyCost.GetResolved() (CardEnergyCost.cs:155-161), which returns the RAW captured value; its only gameplay reader is DanseMacabrePower.cs:24, which is unported (NCardGrid.cs:94,110 is presentation). The sim's single `captured_x` field collapsing the raw and modified values therefore has no observable consequence today; porting Danse Macabre makes it one.
